overall_summary: The channel has extremely low view counts across all initial uploads (5 to 20 views), indicating low algorithmic distribution or early testing phase. Data is insufficient to declare definitive winning patterns, but topics involving phone history, contact names, and late-night overthinking show marginal preference.

winning_patterns.pattern: Phone contact and chat history hooks
winning_patterns.evidence: Video A_eLARoegnw ('आज भी फोन में तुम्हारा नाम सुरक्षित है') got 20 views, the highest in the dataset.
winning_patterns.action: Continue focusing on micro-moments related to smartphones, saved numbers, and chat logs.

weak_patterns.pattern: Vague poetic titles and lengthy hooks
weak_patterns.evidence: Longer introductory phrases like 'Dil Ki Diary: Bewafai Ka Dard...' received lower traction compared to direct situational hooks.
weak_patterns.action: Keep titles short, relatable, and directly tied to the opening line of the hook.

next_video.concept: Typing a long message to an ex at 3 AM and deleting it all before pressing send.
next_video.opening_direction: Start with the sound of typing on a phone screen in a silent room at 3 AM.
next_video.twist_direction: Instead of sending the emotional paragraph, the person just deletes everything and locks the screen, realizing nobody is waiting for that explanation.
next_video.reason: Targets peak late-night overthinking hours when users consume relatable emotional content.

experiment: Testing if a highly visual and universally understood action (typing and deleting a late-night text) improves retention compared to static phone screen text hooks.
